request: The CRM should alert us when our relationship with a country goes cold.
gaps: What specific user roles can see and act on cold relationship alerts?
What happens to alerts when users change roles or leave the organization?
How is engagement activity tracked and recorded in the CRM?
How do we define and handle communication outside the CRM system?
What privacy measures are in place to ensure sensitive information is protected in alert notifications?

proposals.summary: This release delivers an alerting feature that notifies users when engagement activity with a government representative is deemed 'cold'. It is intended for regional coordinators and project managers using the CRM who need timely insights on relationship health.

core_commitments.text: Provide alerts to users when engagement with a country representative has not occurred for a predefined period.
Enable users to configure what constitutes a 'cold' relationship based on the duration of inactivity.

in_scope.text: Implement an alert that triggers if there has been no recorded communication with a country representative for 90 days.
Create a user interface setting that allows regional coordinators and project managers to customize the inactivity threshold from 30 to 180 days.
Include an email notification feature that informs users of a cold relationship when triggered.
Record and display the last engagement date on the country contact profile.
Provide a dashboard view where users can see all relationships that are currently cold.
Ensure alerts comply with data protection regulations regarding sensitive communications.

out_of_scope.text: This release will not include any predictive analytics or recommendations to improve cold relationships.
This release does not address how to re-engage with cold relationships.
The release will not involve tracking communications that happen outside of the CRM system.

assumptions.text: Users have access to the CRM and sufficient permissions to receive alerts and configure settings.
assumptions.why_implicit: The request implies that users will interact with the CRM and utilize its features.

assumptions.text: There is a standard method for tracking engagement activities and recording communication history in the CRM.
assumptions.why_implicit: The request assumes the existence of engagement history data which allows for determining inactivity.

assumptions.text: Users are familiar with how to interpret 'cold' status and take necessary actions based on alerts.
assumptions.why_implicit: The request assumes users will know what to do when alerted about a cold relationship.

definitions.definition: A relationship where there has been no recorded engagement activity or communication for 90 days.
Any recorded communication or interaction with a country representative documented within the CRM.

success_criteria.metric: Percentage of users who receive cold relationship alerts.
success_criteria.target: 80% of users report receiving timely alerts on cold relationships.
success_criteria.measurement: Measured through user feedback surveys within 30 days of release.
